**Finding submitted: deviation (WARRANTY).**

**What the document has.** Section 5 gives only ancillary warranties — legal compliance (5(a)), authority/rights (5(b)), non-infringement (5(c)) and anti-bribery (5(d)) — followed by an "in lieu of all other warranties" disclaimer at 5(e) that strips merchantability and fitness. Section 1(b) requires the Services to be performed "in a professional and workmanlike manner in accordance with industry standards," and Section 4's heading mentions "ACCEPTANCE" but contains no acceptance, conformity or cure mechanic.

**Why it fails the fallback.** There is no warranty that the Services or Works will conform to the Specifications, no warranty period at all (not 12 months, not 90 days, not even 30 days), and no repair/replace/re-performance/refund remedy. With implied warranties disclaimed and no conformance warranty to fall back on, Clear Capital is effectively taking the work as-is — the walk-away outcome in substance, even though the disclaimer is drafted to preserve express warranties.

**Redline (validated ok:true).** Inserted a new Paragraph 5(f) after the disclaimer: professional/workmanlike performance, 90-day conformance to Specifications and documentation for each Work, no malicious code, and a remedy of re-performance, repair/replacement or refund at Contractor's option — plus a sentence confirming 5(e) does not limit these express warranties. The comment flags a 30-day Services period as our available fallback if RadialSpark pushes back.
